Subject: Uptime accounting question for Feb 10 POP maintenance

Hi Tessa,

We reviewed the availability dashboard and the monthly uptime ledger and noticed a discrepancy for our ClearHealth production cluster on 2028-02-10. We had scheduled maintenance across three POPs (SFO, LAX, and PHX) that were staggered over a 6-hour window starting 02/10 01:00 UTC. Our own probes show a period of partial degradation in the west region between 01:45–03:30 UTC (some requests timed out, others succeeded with higher latency).

On Redwood's ledger the event appears as a single aggregated 90-minute degradation and the resulting uptime tally seems lower than we'd expect after accounting for the maintenance windows we published to the maintenance API. Could you clarify how Redwood is apportioning that partial degradation across the POPs and whether the staggered maintenance was excluded in your calculation?

I attached our probe summary (clearhealth_client_probe_summary_20280210.csv) and the incident timeline we put together. If you need any more evidence from our side we can share raw traces.

We'd like either a short explanation of the calculation or a formal credit if the ledger needs adjustment. This affects our monthly SLA reconciliation.

Thanks,
Laura Chen

laura@clearhealth.com

Hi Laura — thanks for the details and the csv. I can confirm we received the maintenance notification for the planned work but I want to make sure we apply our exclusion rules consistently.

High-level: scheduled maintenance that we verified via the maintenance API is generally excluded, but when a maintenance window is staggered across multiple POPs and the customer-facing path remains partially served (i.e., some requests still impacted while others succeed) we run an apportionment step which sometimes results in a reduced exclusion compared to the sum of notified windows.

I'll loop in our SLO accounting team (copying them on this thread) to review the probe evidence and provide a reconstruction of how the 90-minute degradation was derived and whether an adjustment/credit is appropriate. Expect a more detailed response by EOD Monday.

Regards,
Tessa Morgan

Tessa / Marissa — I looked at our telemetry and ran the SLO calculator against the probe data plus Redwood edge logs. Summary below; full workbook attached (slo_calculation_workbook.xlsx) and we zipped the raw evidence (probe_evidence_20280210.zip).

1) Observed timeline (Redwood edge):
- 2028-02-10 01:35–01:55 UTC — progressive latency increase for SFO POP; client path success rate dropped to ~78% for 5m windows.
- 2028-02-10 01:55–02:20 UTC — failover activity: some clients routed to LAX/PHX; combined region success rate ~70%.
- 2028-02-10 02:20–03:30 UTC — intermittent high latency but success rate recovered to ~92% as routing completed.

2) Apportionment and exclusion rules we applied:
- Maintenance exclusions require a maintenance record published to the maintenance API with affected POP list and start/end times. ClearHealth provided an announcement but the recorded affected POP list was SFO and LAX only; PHX appeared in their client notes but not in the maintenance API payload we ingested.
- For staggered maintenance, we compute per-POP impact windows and then aggregate to a regional view using a weighted probe model (each probe weighted by historical path share).
- Partial degradation threshold: we treat a 5-minute window as an outage slot if >=30% of probes fail or if median p95 latency exceeds 3x baseline and error-rate increase is sustained.

3) Why ledger shows ~90 minutes:
- Because PHX was not present in the ingestion payload we only excluded SFO/LAX windows. During the 01:55–02:20 UTC period, failover traffic routed through PHX which caused a region-wide success-rate dip that is not fully covered by the SFO/LAX exclusions. The apportionment step attributes a portion of the impact to non-maintenance-related routing perturbations (routing convergence, peering rate-limits) and thus only ~45 minutes were excluded; the remaining ~45 minutes were counted as degradation.

4) Proposed remediation and next steps:
- If ClearHealth can provide the missing maintenance API payload (or a signed post-facto record) showing PHX as affected with timestamps, we will recompute the ledger and, if appropriate, apply a retroactive maintenance exclusion which would likely restore the uptime to your expected level.
- If the post-facto evidence is insufficient, we can offer a one-time ledger adjustment per the terms in CLH-2028-88 while we update our ingestion checks to flag inconsistencies (we will track this as SUP-2123).

I've attached the workbook that includes the per-probe weighting and the derivation (slo_calculation_workbook.xlsx). Let me know if you'd like a short call to walk through the spreadsheet.

—Kimberly Park
SLO Accounting Lead, Redwood Inference
